title: C1041 — Right-hand headlamp connector
introduction:
The right-hand headlamp has several electrical jobs sharing a housing. I use this reference as a seating chart: the face drawing locates each cavity, while the table explains the circuit assigned to that seat. Begin with the connector identity, find a cavity in the drawing, then read its complete table row rather than stopping at the wire color.

The function descriptions separate low- and high-beam control, relay connections, fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies, park-lamp connections and grounds. A circuit label explains its intended role; it is not evidence that the circuit is working.

The repeated cavity assignment and conflicting counts remain unresolved. This page teaches reference reading, not physical access, probing, diagnosis or replacement. Viewing direction, test values, gauge conventions and the meanings of the Size and Used codes are not established here. The metadata Pin Count differs from the cavity count shown by the drawing and the pigtail record; the source does not reconcile that difference.

edits.why: The printed drawing places the lower-numbered column on the right and the higher-numbered column on the left, with numbers decreasing downward. I use those printed labels to find the matching Cavity entry. Outlined circles correspond to rows carrying circuit descriptions, while gray-filled circles correspond to rows without them; the shading does not report electrical health. The side projections help distinguish the drawn housing shape, but they are not identified as release or locking mechanisms. The drawing also leaves the physical viewing direction unspecified.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: Keep each row intact when reading across Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Terminal Part Number. Control-module, relay, supply and ground descriptions identify different circuit roles. A relay lets an electrical command switch another circuit, although the label does not establish a removable relay. Preserve the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternatives rather than assuming a fuse. The repeated cavity entry carries different circuit and color descriptions with no qualifier to distinguish applicability; it cannot be resolved by choosing whichever row looks more familiar.

This is the lookup record for the listed connector repair lead. Number, Service Part and Engineering Shell are separate identification fields; I compare their labels before treating an entry as a part reference. Gauge, Material, Cavities and Image describe that listed pigtail. They do not establish a wire-selection or installation procedure, and the conflicting connector and pigtail counts remain open for review.
The regional Product Id is an additional lookup reference. Its presence does not settle vehicle applicability, interchangeability or the method of installing a replacement.

originalAuthorHold: Pin Count is 17, while the face drawing labels cavities 1–16 and the pigtail table specifies 16 cavities. These counts are not reconciled.

Cavity 10 has both CLF31, YE-GY, for the right low-beam relay connection and SBB35, BU-RD, for a fuse-35-or-circuit-breaker supply. The Qualifier cells are blank, leaving configuration alternatives versus an erroneous assignment unresolved.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 49 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 4 edits. Count and repeated cavity relay/supply assignment ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
